description: The XREFFILE browse, pinned as the five CALLs CBSTM03A makes to read a cross-reference file end to end: one OPEN, three READs and one CLOSE. Dispatch. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD at app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118 selects WHEN 'XREFFILE' at :121 and performs 2000-XREFFILE-PROC THRU 2999-EXIT at :122. That arm is the SECOND of the four, so every call here proves the ordered EVALUATE reaches it rather than stopping at 'TRNXFILE' (gate G30); the same five images would be indistinguishable under an unordered dispatch only if the DD they each carry were ignored, and LK-M03B-DD pins it. The guarded paragraph. 2000-XREFFILE-PROC (:157-179) is three independent guards, each of which exits the moment it fires: IF M03B-OPEN at :159 does OPEN INPUT XREF-FILE at :160 then GO TO 2900-EXIT at :161; IF M03B-READ at :164 does READ XREF-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT at :165-166 then GO TO 2900-EXIT at :167; IF M03B-CLOSE at :170 does CLOSE XREF-FILE at :171 then GO TO 2900-EXIT at :172. All three converge on 2900-EXIT (:175-176), whose single statement is MOVE XREFFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC, and then on 2999-EXIT (:178-179). Every LK-M03B-RC of '00' below is therefore that one MOVE, reading the XREFFILE-STATUS area declared at :87-89 - a two-byte area of its own, distinct from the TRNXFILE-STATUS at :83-85, which is why statuses are driven per DD rather than globally (gate G47). The caller idiom transcribed. Call one is 8200-XREFFILE-OPEN (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:765-769): MOVE 'XREFFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD, SET M03B-OPEN TO TRUE, MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC, CALL 'CBSTM03B' USING WS-M03B-AREA. Calls two to four are 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT (:345-351), which is the only one of the three paragraphs that also issues MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:350) - so each READ starts from a cleared record area. Call five is 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE (:873-877), which resets the status but NOT the record area; that is why the CLOSE image still carries the third record in LK-M03B-FLDT rather than spaces, and reproducing that residue is the point of pinning it. The OPEN and the CLOSE are accepted by the caller at :771 and :879 on '00' OR '04', so '00' is one of two values that continue there; the READ is accepted only on '00' (:354-355), takes end of file on '10' (:356-357), and abends on anything else (:358-361). Order is the behaviour. SELECT XREF-FILE declares ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL over RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-CARD-NUM (:37-41), so three READs return three rows in ascending key order: card numbers 0500024453765740, then 0683586198171516, then 0923877193247330. The seed app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt is already stored in that order, which is what a KSDS guarantees, so the case pins the ORDER of the browse and not merely its contents - a unit that returned the same three rows in another sequence fails here. Because the access mode is sequential, no keyed read is involved: LK-M03B-KEY stays twenty-five spaces and LK-M03B-KEY-LN stays the zoned image of zero, '000{', whose trailing brace is a positive-sign overpunch in the low-order byte of PIC S9(4) and not a stray character. Widths, re-derivable by hand (practice B11). Each area image is 1040 bytes because LK-M03B-AREA (:100-112) is 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000; the six spans are named individually below so all 1040 bytes are asserted field by field and not only as one string (gate G17). READ ... INTO LK-M03B-FLDT at :165 is a PIC X MOVE of a 50-byte record into a 1000-byte receiver, so a READ image is the 50 record bytes followed by 950 spaces. Each cross-reference row is 50 bytes because app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy is 16 + 9 + 11 + a trailing FILLER X(14). Code page, named and never inferred (practice B8). Every byte above is US-ASCII, which is the code page of the authoritative fixtures under app/data/ASCII; IBM037 is the code page of the reference-only EBCDIC datasets under app/data/EBCDIC and is deliberately not used here. The platform default is never relied on, which matters for the one character in this case that is not a digit or a space: the '{' of LK-M03B-KEY-LN is 0x7B in US-ASCII and would be a different byte entirely under an EBCDIC reading. The 36-versus-50 deviation (gate G16, risk R-F). cardxref.txt ships 36 bytes per record - XREF-CARD-NUM, XREF-CUST-ID and XREF-ACCT-ID and nothing more - where CVACT03Y declares 50 including that trailing FILLER. This case therefore declares the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation against XREFFILE and leaves the seed at its shipped width: inputs is fixture-backed, so no row is written out here at all and nothing in this file can pre-pad one. The absent fourteen spaces are supplied once, at seed time, by the harness that owns that pad, before anything decodes a row. Naming FILLER explicitly in each final-state row is the field-level proof that they arrived: it is precisely the span the fixture omits, and a pad applied twice or not at all shows up there first. Read-only, proved twice. All four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph in CBSTM03B writes, so the three seeded rows must come back exactly as they went in. That is asserted row by row in expectedFinalState and again at dataset level in expectedDatasets, where XREFFILE is pinned at three rows of 50 bytes on the FINAL_STATE channel - a count and a width no row expectation can state on its own. Return code and messages. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference anywhere and simply GOBACKs at :130-131; LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS, not the return code, and the two are deliberately not conflated. expectedMessages is empty because the subroutine contains no DISPLAY statement at all - 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' at CBSTM03A.CBL:359 belongs to the caller. Two operation codes stay dark (practice B5). M03B-WRITE 'W' and M03B-REWRITE 'Z' are declared at :107-108 but are never SET anywhere in app/cbl, so no case drives them as a successful operation and this one does not either; they remain declared and unexercised rather than being invented into life. The unit (gate G12, requirement I3, practice B4). The prompt-mandated Java name is StatementGenerationJobB, but CBSTM03B is not a job: its own header at :7 reads 'BATCH COBOL Subroutine', no EXEC PGM=CBSTM03B appears in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and CBSTM03A CALLs it thirteen times. It is therefore a Spring @Component and unitKind is COMPONENT. The name divergence is recorded here rather than quietly corrected. The component is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). Provenance (practice B12). Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - from the line numbers cited here, from the CVACT03Y field offsets, and from the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt - and was NEVER captured from a COBOL execution. No COBOL runs in this environment: AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, among them a COBOL compiler whose indexed file handler is disabled, which is exactly what an ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED file like this one would need. The deviation is one of provenance only - twenty cases, field-for-field diffing and a diff count of zero all stand - and it is escalated as risk R-A in AAP section 0.9.11. HOW THE CALL SCRIPT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HELD IN JAVA: the sequence of CALLs below used to live in a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant the case file did not describe the one thing it asserts - a subroutine whose entire contract is a DD name plus a one-character operation code IS its call sequence. Renumbering this file would have silently given it a different script, and a twenty-first case would have thrown from a default arm. unitStimulus.operationScript now carries it, one entry per CALL in issue order, each declaring LK-M03B-DD, the 88-level operation code from app/cbl/CBSTM03B.cbl:103-108, and where applicable LK-M03B-KEY and LK-M03B-KEY-LN. Two caller idioms are declared explicitly because the source distinguishes them: status '00' is the MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC every real call site issues, and its ABSENCE carries the previous call's status forward - the only way to observe a fall-through exit that assigns nothing new; primesRecordArea true is the MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT that app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L350, :L745 and :L834 issue, and its ABSENCE is the omission at :L857-860 that makes 'at end of file the record area is returned unchanged' an assertion with content. Every expected area image below was derived from this script by reading CBSTM03B's rules, never by running the Java.
